events.speaker: CONSTANCE
events.text: Your third column has not balanced since April. Over a shilling I would have kept quiet. It is not a shilling, it is eleven dollars and forty cents, and it goes astray in the same week of every month, which is the part that ought to interest you.

events.speaker: CONSTANCE
events.text: Here. The same hand wrote both entries and only one of them reached the tally. That is not arithmetic giving out. Arithmetic does not grow tired on the second Tuesday and recover by the third.

events.speaker: CONSTANCE
events.text: I want no fee for it. I want standing leave to read every page before you put your name to anything, and I want you to stop putting your name to things by lamplight when you are tired.

events.speaker: CONSTANCE
events.text: I take my spectacles off to make a point. I have been taking them off in front of you when there is no point whatever to be made, and I am too precise a woman not to have noticed.
